# Skill Overview: Employment Contract Templates

Here is a comprehensive summary of the skill documentation and a tailored workflow for creating your senior software engineer offer letter.

---

## Documentation Overview

### Purpose of the Skill

Create employment contracts, offer letters, and HR policy documents following legal best practices. This skill is active whenever you are drafting employment agreements, creating HR policies, or standardizing employment documentation.

### Document Types Covered

| Document | Purpose | When Used |
|----------|---------|-----------|
| **Offer Letter** | Initial job offer | Pre-hire |
| **Employment Contract** | Formal agreement | Hire |
| **Employee Handbook** | Policies & procedures | Onboarding |
| **NDA** | Confidentiality | Before access |
| **Non-Compete** | Competition restriction | Hire/Exit |

### Core Legal Concepts to Keep in Mind

```
Employment Relationship:
├── At-Will vs. Contract
├── Employee vs. Contractor
├── Full-Time vs. Part-Time
├── Exempt vs. Non-Exempt
└── Jurisdiction-Specific Requirements
```

### Best Practices

**Do's:**
- **Consult legal counsel** — Employment law varies by jurisdiction
- **Keep copies signed** — Document all agreements
- **Update regularly** — Laws and policies change
- **Be clear and specific** — Avoid ambiguity
- **Train managers** — On policies and procedures

**Don'ts:**
- **Don't use generic templates** — Customize for your jurisdiction
- **Don't make promises** — That could create implied contracts
- **Don't discriminate** — In language or application
- **Don't forget at-will language** — Where applicable
- **Don't skip review** — Have legal counsel review all documents

---

## Workflow for Creating a Senior Software Engineer Offer Letter

Follow this step-by-step process using the **Offer Letter** template from the skill:

### Step 1: Gather Position Details

Before drafting, collect the following specifics for the senior software engineer role:

| Data Point | Example |
|---|---|
| **Job Title** | Senior Software Engineer |
| **Department** | Engineering / Product Development |
| **Reports To** | VP of Engineering / Engineering Manager |
| **Location** | Office location or Remote (note if remote-first) |
| **Start Date** | As mutually agreed |
| **Employment Type** | Full-Time, Exempt (salaried engineers are typically exempt) |
| **Salary** | Market rate for senior engineer + seniority factor |
| **Bonus** | e.g., 10–15% target annual bonus |
| **Equity** | e.g., stock options with 4-year vesting / 1-year cliff |
| **Benefits** | Medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match, PTO |

### Step 2: Apply the Offer Letter Template Structure

Use the template sections in order:

1. **Header** — Company letterhead, date, candidate name/address
2. **Opening paragraph** — Position offered + positive framing
3. **Position Details table** — Title, department, reporting line, location, start date
4. **Compensation** — Base salary, bonus eligibility, equity grant
5. **Benefits** — Standard package summary + effective dates
6. **Contingencies** — Background check, right-to-work verification, required signed documents (Confidentiality Agreement, IP Assignment Agreement — critical for engineers!)
7. **At-Will Employment statement** (if in an at-will jurisdiction)
8. **Acceptance section** — Signature lines, deadline for acceptance

### Step 3: Customize for the Engineering Role

For a **senior software engineer**, pay special attention to:

- **Intellectual Property / IP Assignment** — Emphasize that they will sign an IP assignment agreement as a contingency. Even in the offer letter, this signals that all code and inventions produced will be company property.
- **Confidentiality Agreement** — Include as a required signed document (source code, architecture plans, trade secrets).
- **Equity/Stock Options** — Senior engineering offers frequently include equity. Reference the separate Stock Option Agreement to avoid putting vesting terms that could create unintended contractual obligations in the offer letter itself.
- **Remote/Flexibility** — If the role is remote or hybrid, be explicit about the location expectation.
- **Exempt vs. Non-Exempt** — Confirm "Exempt" status (salaried, not eligible for overtime) which aligns with professional engineering roles.

### Step 4: Draft with Legal Precautions

- Include **"this offer letter does not constitute a contract of employment for any specific period"** language to maintain at-will status.
- Refer to equity terms as governed by a **separate agreement**.
- Put **any bonus as discretionary**, tied to company and individual performance.
- Keep the offer **contingent** on background check and right-to-work verification.
- Set an **offer expiration date** (typically 5–10 business days).
- Add the **disclaimer** that the document is not legal advice and recommend HR/legal review.

### Step 5: Review Checklist Before Sending

- [ ] All bracketed placeholders `[X]` replaced with real values
- [ ] Salary/equity numbers confirmed and approved
- [ ] Reporting manager title correct
- [ ] Start date aligned with the candidate
- [ ] Jurisdiction-appropriate at-will language included
- [ ] Contingencies reflect company policy (background check, IP assignment, etc.)
- [ ] Benefits summary matches current HR offerings
- [ ] Acceptance deadline set
- [ ] Reviewed by HR/Legal (per best practice)

### Step 6: Post-Acceptance

After the candidate signs, ensure the following downstream documents are prepared (per the skill's document types):

1. **Formal Employment Agreement** (Template 2) — for the hire file, including IP assignment provisions in detail
2. **NDA / Confidentiality Agreement** — executed before granting source code access
3. **Employee Handbook acknowledgment** — during onboarding
4. **Non-Compete / Non-Solicitation** (if applicable in your jurisdiction) — negotiated separately at hire

---

## Key Sections from the Template (Quick Reference)

The full **Offer Letter** template in the skill includes these essential blocks you'll populate:

```
## Position Details
Title / Department / Reports To / Location / Start Date / Employment Type

## Compensation
Base Salary: $[AMOUNT] per [year], paid [frequency]
Bonus: Eligible up to X% [or Not applicable]
Equity: [Options with vesting] [or Not applicable]

## Benefits
- Health insurance effective [date]
- 401(k) with [X]% match
- PTO days / holidays
- [Other benefits]

## Contingencies
- Background check
- Right to work in [country]
- Confidentiality Agreement
- IP Assignment Agreement

## At-Will Employment
[Statement that either party may terminate at any time]

## Acceptance
Signature lines + offer expiration deadline
```
